hypothesis: The v2 StateRootIdentity layer (src/frankenstein2/state_migration.py, class StateRootIdentity, method assert_eligible_canonical_root) can recognize/validate the EXACT existing real path of the local v1 unified.db as a canonical state root, without changing the file and without creating a second DB.

module_source_review.finding: Zero filesystem or OS I/O in the module: no open(), no os.* calls anywhere in the file. Only pathlib.PurePosixPath string manipulation, dataclasses, hashlib.sha256 over caller-supplied in-memory dict content, and re for format checks. Confirmed safe to import and call directly against the real db path with no risk of writing to it.

action_performed.method: python3 -c '...' importing StateRootIdentity from src/frankenstein2/state_migration.py, called from ~/frankenstein-2.0

inputs.host_identity_sha256: sha256 of a fixed local literal string, computed inline, not a secret/env value
inputs.observed_root_fingerprint_sha256: aeaf5304f70242bf385c7dd9af21c7c96b94735810daad172e7b7ce465c35308 (the db file's own pre-test SHA-256, passed in as a literal, not re-read from disk inside the module)

measurement.db_fingerprint_delta: NONE — size, mtime and SHA-256 identical before and after; unified.db was not touched by this test.

what_changed: Nothing on disk. One Python process ran, imported a pure-validation module, constructed one in-memory dataclass instance, computed one SHA-256 digest of that in-memory dict, and returned.
what_did_not_change: unified.db bytes, mtime, inode, table list, git state of ~/frankenstein-2.0 (aside from this run's own new files), git state of ~/frankenstein-repo, any systemd/process state, main branch anywhere.
scope_caveat_important: PASS means the class ACCEPTS a caller-supplied claim that this path+storage_class combination is a canonical root, and that acceptance is a real, meaningful validation (it does reject transient-looking paths like /tmp, /var/tmp, /run, /dev/shm or anything with a .cache path segment, and it does reject storage_class values other than CANONICAL_DURABLE). It is NOT autonomous discovery: the module has no code that inspects the host filesystem, stat()s the path, or independently infers storage_class. The caller (this test, in future any real integration code) must supply path and storage_class as explicit claims. This is consistent with the module's own docstring: 'deliberately plan-only ... does not touch the filesystem, inspect a host, mutate UnifiedDB'.
counterhypotheses_considered: Maybe assert_eligible_canonical_root() would accept ANY plausible-looking absolute path regardless of correctness, making this a weak test. Partially true: it only rejects the transient-path patterns hardcoded in _is_obviously_transient() (/tmp, /var/tmp, /run, /dev/shm, any '.cache' path segment) plus non-CANONICAL_DURABLE storage_class. A path like /home/foo/bar/nonexistent-file also passes structurally (no filesystem existence check at all). So this discriminator proves *structural compatibility of the real unified.db path with v2's canonical-root shape*, not that v2 has verified the file actually exists or is a valid SQLite DB.

Maybe host_identity_sha256 should be derived from a real, reproducible host-identity scheme rather than an arbitrary literal. This run used an arbitrary fixed string purely to satisfy the SHA-256 hex format requirement; no real host-identity derivation scheme was found or invented. A real integration would need the coordinator/architecture to define what host_identity_sha256 canonically means.
next_exact_action_if_authorized: Do NOT proceed with StateLineage/StateMigrationRequest/StateMigrationPlan construction (that requires deciding a real lineage_id/generation/state_sha256 scheme for unified.db and a target_root, which starts to look like real migration planning, not just root-shape validation) without explicit coordinator authorization, since it edges toward defining a second root (target_root) even in plan-only form.
